newsitem.title: USA: Bank of Montreal trims N.Y. forex staff.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Montreal trims N.Y. forex staff.

text.p: Bank of Montreal, one of North America's 10 largest commercial banks, reduced its foreign exchange staff in New York by four people on Monday, according to the firm's global head of currency trading.

The layoffs included three sales persons and one administrative staff member, trimming the New York sales force to eight, said Jamie Thorsen, senior vice president of global foreign exchange in Chicago.

"We combined two offices in New York and we thought through natural attrition we would get it down to a number that was more sensible ... but it just didn't happen," Thorsen said, explaining the reason behind Monday's cutbacks.
Bank of Montreal and its Chicago-based subsidiary Harris Bank merged their foreign exchange operations in 1995.
All U.S. trading staff are located in Chicago.
Asked about further reductions in the midwest near-term, Thorsen declined to comment.
